description: Experience the true taste of Liguria with our Focaccia Genovese, a masterpiece of Italian baking. This beloved flatbread boasts a delightfully airy crumb, a crisp golden crust, and is infused with fragrant rosemary and the finest olive oil. Perfect as an appetizer, side, or a light meal, it brings the warmth of Italy to your table.

ingredients.notes: plus extra for drizzling and pan

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine the warm water, active dry yeast, and granulated sugar. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour and fine sea salt. Pour the activated yeast mixture and 2 tablespoons (30ml) of the extra virgin olive oil into the flour. Mix with a spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Transfer to a lightly floured surface.

instructions.title: Knead and First Rise
instructions.text: Knead the dough for 8-10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic. It should be slightly sticky. Lightly oil a clean bowl with olive oil, place the dough inside, turn to coat, then cover with plastic wrap. Let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Prepare for Baking
instructions.text: Generously drizzle 3 tablespoons (45ml) of extra virgin olive oil into a 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking pan. Gently transfer the risen dough into the pan. Do not punch it down. Gently stretch the dough with your fingertips to fill the pan, being careful not to tear it.

instructions.title: Dimple and Second Rise
instructions.text: Using your fingertips, create characteristic dimples all over the surface of the dough. Drizzle the remaining 1 tablespoon (15ml) of olive oil over the dimpled dough. Sprinkle evenly with the coarse sea salt and fresh rosemary leaves. Cover lightly with plastic wrap and let it rise again for 30-45 minutes.

instructions.title: Bake to Golden Perfection
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 220C (425F) during the last 15 minutes of the second rise. Bake the focaccia for 20-25 minutes, or until it is golden brown on top and cooked through. The bottom should also be golden.

instructions.title: Serve and Enjoy
instructions.text: Once out of the oven, immediately drizzle with a final touch of fresh extra virgin olive oil for added flavor and shine. Let it cool in the pan for a few minutes before transferring to a wire rack. Slice and serve warm.

tips: For an extra airy focaccia, use a high-hydration dough. This recipe uses a good amount of water, but you can increase it slightly if you are comfortable working with stickier dough.
Do not skip the second rise. This is crucial for developing the characteristic airy texture and deep flavor of authentic Focaccia Genovese.
Always use good quality extra virgin olive oil, both in the dough and for drizzling. It is a key flavor component for this recipe.
Do not overbake the focaccia; it should be golden brown and soft, not hard and dry. The internal temperature should be around 90-95C (195-205F).
article:
The enticing aroma of freshly baked bread, infused with fragrant rosemary and rich olive oil, is a quintessential experience in Italian baking. Among the pantheon of Italy’s beloved breads, Focaccia Genovese stands out as a true masterpiece – a simple yet profoundly satisfying flatbread hailing from the Liguria region. Its distinctive dimpled surface, glistening with extra virgin olive oil, and its irresistible combination of a crisp crust and a soft, airy interior, make it a universal favorite. This isn't just bread; it's a sensory journey to the sun-drenched coasts of Genoa, a testament to the power of a few humble ingredients transformed into something extraordinary. If you've ever dreamt of mastering the art of Italian baking, tackling the Focaccia Genovese recipe is an excellent place to start, promising delicious rewards for your efforts.

## What is Focaccia Genovese?
Focaccia Genovese, or "fugassa" as it's known in the local Ligurian dialect, is more than just a type of focaccia; it's the original, the benchmark against which all other focaccias are measured. Originating from Genoa, the capital of Liguria, this flatbread has a history stretching back centuries, believed to have been a simple bread baked on hearths before ovens became common. What distinguishes the Genovese version is its characteristic thinness compared to other focaccias, its incredibly generous application of extra virgin olive oil both within the dough and on its surface, and the signature deep dimples that catch pools of oil and coarse sea salt.

Unlike some chewier, thicker focaccias, the Genovese style prides itself on a delicate balance: a golden, slightly crunchy crust that gives way to an interior that is remarkably soft, tender, and riddled with air pockets. The liberal use of high-quality olive oil isn't just for flavor; it contributes significantly to the bread's texture, keeping it moist and preventing it from drying out. Often adorned simply with fresh rosemary and coarse sea salt, its beauty lies in its elegant simplicity, allowing the quality of its core ingredients to shine through. Understanding these nuances is key to a successful Focaccia Genovese recipe.

## Ingredients for Focaccia Genovese
The beauty of the Focaccia Genovese recipe lies in its minimalist ingredient list, emphasizing quality over quantity. Each component plays a crucial role in achieving that authentic taste and texture.

*   **"00" Flour (or All-Purpose Flour):** While "00" flour is traditional for its fine texture and low protein content, a good quality all-purpose flour works perfectly well. The key is consistency and the ability to absorb water for a well-hydrated dough.
*   **Water:** Lukewarm water is essential for activating the yeast. The exact amount can vary slightly depending on your flour, but the dough should be quite wet and sticky.
*   **Fresh Yeast (or Active Dry Yeast):** Fresh yeast provides a subtle, nuanced flavor, but active dry yeast is a perfectly acceptable substitute. Ensure it's fresh and active for a good rise.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil:** This is the star ingredient. Do not skimp on quality here. A good, fruity extra virgin olive oil from Italy will lend its characteristic flavor and contribute significantly to the focaccia's texture, both inside and out.
*   **Fine Sea Salt:** Incorporated into the dough for flavor.
*   **Coarse Sea Salt:** Crucial for sprinkling on top before baking. These larger crystals provide bursts of salty crunch that contrast beautifully with the soft bread.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** The aromatic hero. Fresh rosemary sprigs, picked and gently pressed into the dough, release their essential oils during baking, infusing the focaccia with its signature herbaceous fragrance and taste.

## How to Make Focaccia Genovese: Step-by-Step
Creating this iconic Italian bread is a rewarding experience. Below, we'll walk you through the authentic Focaccia Genovese recipe, step-by-step, ensuring you achieve that perfect balance of crispy, airy, and intensely flavorful.

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine the lukewarm water with a pinch of sugar (to feed the yeast) and crumble in the fresh yeast (or sprinkle active dry yeast). Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
2.  **Mix the Dough:** Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Pour in about half of the extra virgin olive oil. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms.
3.  **Knead (Lightly):** Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface. Knead for about 5-7 minutes. The dough will be quite wet and sticky, but resist the urge to add too much flour. A wet dough leads to a tender focaccia. You can use a stand mixer with a dough hook for 5 minutes if preferred.
4.  **First Rise:** Lightly grease a clean bowl with olive oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turn it once to coat, and cover with plastic wrap or a damp cloth. Let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.
5.  **Prepare the Pan:** Liberally grease a standard baking sheet (approx. 13x18 inches or similar) with plenty of extra virgin olive oil. Don't be shy; this creates the crispy bottom crust.
6.  **Shape and Dimple:** Gently transfer the risen dough to the oiled baking sheet. Without deflating it too much, gently stretch it with your fingertips to cover the entire pan. This may take a few minutes. Let it rest for 10 minutes if it resists stretching. Once it covers the pan, use your fingertips to create deep, characteristic dimples across the entire surface.
7.  **Second Rise:** Drizzle generously with more extra virgin olive oil, ensuring it pools in the dimples. Sprinkle with fresh rosemary leaves and coarse sea salt. Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap and let it rise again for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
8.  **Bake:** Preheat your oven to a high temperature, around 425°F (220°C). Bake for 20-30 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown on top and the bottom is crispy and golden.
9.  **Cool and Serve:** Once baked, immediately transfer the focaccia to a wire rack to cool slightly. Drizzle with a tiny bit more olive oil if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature.

## Tips for Perfect Focaccia Genovese
Achieving that authentic Ligurian focaccia experience involves a few key considerations that elevate your Focaccia Genovese recipe from good to extraordinary.

*   **Quality Ingredients are Non-Negotiable:** This cannot be stressed enough, especially for the extra virgin olive oil and fresh rosemary. Their flavors are prominent, so choose the best you can find.
*   **Hydration is Key:** Focaccia Genovese dough is meant to be very wet, almost sticky. This high hydration is what contributes to its characteristic airy, open crumb. Resist the urge to add too much extra flour during kneading or shaping.
*   **Don't Skimp on the Olive Oil:** From oiling the bowl to greasing the pan, incorporating it into the dough, and drizzling it over the top before baking – olive oil is fundamental. It prevents sticking, adds flavor, and creates that irresistible crispy exterior.
*   **Embrace the Dimples:** Those deep indentations are not just for aesthetics. They create pockets for the olive oil and salt to collect, intensifying the flavor and texture in those spots. Don't be afraid to press firmly with your fingertips.
*   **Patience with Rising:** Allow the dough ample time for both rises. A slow, proper fermentation develops flavor and ensures a light, airy texture.
*   **Hot Oven, Quick Bake:** A high oven temperature helps create a quick, crisp crust while keeping the interior soft. Keep an eye on it to prevent over-browning.
*   **Listen to Your Dough:** Learn to feel the dough. If it's too stiff, a little more water might be needed. If it's too slack, a tiny bit of flour could help, but generally, err on the side of wetness.
*   **Use a Metal Pan:** A dark metal baking sheet conducts heat well, helping to achieve that coveted crispy, golden bottom crust.

## Serving Suggestions for Focaccia
Once you've mastered the Focaccia Genovese recipe, the serving possibilities are endless, reflecting its versatility in Italian cuisine.

*   **Simple Snack:** Enjoy it plain, perhaps with a morning coffee or as an afternoon pick-me-up, just as they do in Genoa. The flavor is rich enough to stand on its own.
*   **Dipping:** Serve alongside a small bowl of high-quality extra virgin olive oil, perhaps with a splash of balsamic vinegar, for dipping.
*   **Antipasto Platter:** A perfect accompaniment to cured meats like prosciutto or salami, and a selection of Italian cheeses such as fresh mozzarella, provolone, or parmesan.
*   **Sandwiches:** Its sturdy yet soft texture makes focaccia an excellent bread for sandwiches. Fill it with grilled vegetables, roasted chicken, or classic Italian cold cuts.
*   **Accompaniment to Meals:** Serve it alongside hearty soups, stews, or fresh salads. It's fantastic for soaking up delicious broths and dressings.
*   **Bruschetta Base:** Toast slices lightly and top with fresh tomatoes, basil, and garlic for a twist on bruschetta.
*   **Pizza Alternative:** While not pizza, a slice of focaccia topped with some fresh tomato sauce and mozzarella can make for a quick and satisfying snack.

## Variations & Substitutions
While the classic Focaccia Genovese recipe is beloved, there's always room for creative variations to suit different tastes or dietary needs.

*   **Toppings Galore:** Beyond rosemary, consider adding other traditional Italian toppings. Cherry tomatoes, sliced black olives, thinly sliced onions, or even a sprinkle of oregano can be pressed into the dough before the second rise.
*   **Herb Combinations:** Experiment with other fresh herbs. Thyme, sage, or a mix of Italian herbs can add different aromatic profiles.
*   **Garlic Infusion:** Mince a few cloves of garlic and mix them with some olive oil to drizzle over the focaccia before baking for a pungent kick.
*   **Cheese Topping:** A light sprinkle of grated Parmesan or Pecorino Romano cheese can be added during the last few minutes of baking for a cheesy crust.
*   **Whole Wheat Flour:** For a healthier twist, substitute up to 25-30% of the "00" or all-purpose flour with whole wheat flour. This will result in a denser bread with a nuttier flavor.
*   **Gluten-Free Options:** While a true Focaccia Genovese relies on wheat flour, many gluten-free flour blends are now available that can yield surprisingly good results for focaccia-style breads. Look for blends designed for yeast baking.
*   **Olive Oil Infusions:** Infuse your olive oil with chili flakes or lemon zest beforehand to add another layer of flavor.

Focaccia Genovese with rosemary and olive oil is more than just bread; it's an emblem of Italian culinary tradition, a celebration of simple ingredients yielding profound flavor. Its crispy crust, airy interior, and aromatic embrace of rosemary and extra virgin olive oil make it an irresistible delight. By following this comprehensive Focaccia Genovese recipe, you're not just baking; you're embarking on a delightful culinary journey, bringing the authentic taste of Liguria into your home. So roll up your sleeves, embrace the stickiness of the dough, and prepare to be rewarded with one of the most satisfying breads you’ll ever bake. Buon appetito!
